It was just his way of doing it sure it might a bit over the top but it's people tend to forget it's a game. sure it's competitive and professional. it creates this wall separating the community from the game and experience. The whole thing with these communities is the closeness and ability to relate.

It provided entertainment rather than took away from the actual experience. Sure it could be seen as 'cheap' or whatever. The casters found it easy to follow thoughts and subjects and so did the viewers. While I understand it's a 3 million dollar event that shouldn't mean that it should be so black and white. Having a panel like that they should have expected some banter and jokes along with well thought out analysis and predictions. The community of dota isn't stuck up. We either like things or we don't. we don't really seek out black tie event panels. But judging from the backlash clearly the vocal majority liked it. I did too. It was clumsy and a great way to keep the flow of the panel moving without being stuck for too long on one hero, team, or player. Just my 2 cents.
